what_it_does: This paper describes a high-capacity magnetic memory chip (64 gigabits—enough for several feature films)—built using a cross-point architecture where tiny magnetic junctions sit at the intersection of rows and columns. The magnetic state (which direction the magnetization points) stores a 0 or 1. The challenge is reliably reading the magnetic state without accidentally flipping it. The paper proposes a timing-controlled discharge-read scheme that carefully manages electrical discharging to maximize the signal you can detect from the magnetic junction while minimizing accidental bit flips.
